title: Sonar (LEGO US from set 8547, ~20 y/o) reads 255 (no echo) constantly - presumed dead
notes:
2026-10-25: the sonar reads 255 (no echo) at rest at the repositioned robot - confirmed by a direct one-shot BrickPi read AND the running wrapper (the color sensor on the neighboring PORT_1 reads 776 fine, zero errors). User verdict: the sensor is ~20 years old (the original Mindstorms set) and can simply be broken. Optional revival path: check the PORT_4 wire/aim. All the sonar-dependent measurement plans switched to the kinect depth oracle.
2026-10-25 user hypothesis: the sonar may be aimed OUT OF RANGE or at a grazing angle (reads 255 = no echo either way) rather than dead. Supporting: the kinect sees the obstacle at 0.67-0.87 m - well inside the LEGO US ~5-250 cm envelope - so an aimed-at-obstacle sonar should echo. Differential test (user, physical): place a solid target ~30 cm directly in front of the transducer at rest and re-read; still 255 => dead/wire.
close_reason: Not dead: reads a steady 61 cm with the obstacle at 0.61-0.67 m (Kinect) on 2026-10-26. The earlier 255 readings fit the user's aim/range hypothesis (plus the known blindness while tracks turn).

title: Mission: drive motor gear ratio via forward/backward sonar ranging
description: Determine the drive-train calibration: drive the robot forward/backward to the same spot (encoder-driven legs) and read the displacement from the chassis-mounted sonar (obstacle 75 cm dead-ahead = position oracle). Yields ticks/cm of travel (the odometry constant bundling gear ratio + track sprocket diameter), the forward/backward asymmetry (drivetrain backlash/slip), and the left/right symmetry. Kinect depth cross-checks the distances. The true motor:sprocket ratio needs the sprocket diameter measured separately.
notes:
2026-10-25: the rear track BROKE mid-run (all run-1 data invalid, retracted). Valid findings: the drive train is geared ~6x deeper than the turret (~1.16 ticks/s per speed unit vs 7.2 - the legs must budget at the drive rate); the sonar is blind WHILE the tracks turn (EMI/vibration) and only works at rest; the kinect depth works during motion but the USB storms gap it. After the repair + repositioning the obstacle is at 43 cm (sonar) / 0.50 m (kinect) - too close for 15 cm excursions. BLOCKED on the user repositioning the robot to ~75-80 cm with >=40 cm clear behind.
2026-10-25 v4 run blocked: the sonar reads 255 (no echo) AT REST at the repositioned robot - confirmed by a direct one-shot BrickPi read (the color sensor on PORT_1 reads 776 fine, zero wrapper errors). Likely the PORT_4 wire knocked loose during the track repair, or the sonar's aim changed with the repositioning. v4 probe (sonar oracle, encoder-driven blind legs, at-rest sonar verification) deployed and ready; a kinect-oracle variant is the fallback (the kinect sees ~0.8 m at rest; its post-motion recovery is ~13-16 s per measurement).
2026-10-25: the sonar written off (koc-hw-sonar-dead). The mission proceeds with the KINECT depth as the sole oracle (+-1-3 mm at 0.5-1 m per the FrameProcessor docstring - better than the sonar's +-1 cm), with ~16 s post-motion recovery waits per measurement (the USB respawn cycle after the vibration-induced storms).
2026-10-25 MISSION COMPLETE (v5, kinect oracle): ticks/cm = 161.0 +- 0.2 (three 20 cm legs, 0.2 percent spread; the rate blip 153.6 within the kinect accuracy); the drivetrain backlash/slip < 0.4 cm per 40 cm round trip; GoForward = toward the obstacle, the left encoder negative / the right positive on forward. The kinect recovery waits (~16 s per measurement) had zero losses in ~10 min. The true motor:sprocket ratio needs the sprocket diameter (161 ticks/cm = 2.24 cm of travel per motor rev; ~7.6:1 at a 17 cm sprocket).

Mission: 90-degree turret swing reliability (encoder/color/kinect)
description: Test whether the turret can reliably swing +/-90 deg off center and return: cable limits and stall behavior, encoder drift/backlash over large excursions, the color fingerprint beyond the mapped range, kinect scene verification. Robot static. Sensors: encoder (PORT_C), color (PORT_1), sonar (PORT_4, 75 cm obstacle ground truth), kinect depth. Ratio caveat: 125 ticks/deg is +-10 percent, so legs are encoder-driven (stop on reached ticks), not time-driven.
notes:
2026-10-25 mission complete: +90/-180/+90 encoder-driven legs all 100% of target, no stalls, no cable limits in the +-90 span; return error 6 ticks (0.05 deg) after fixing the command-queue backlog (stream at the 0.3 s consumption rate). Color fingerprint reproduced exactly (768->768) and spans 734-768 across +-90 deg; sonar 75 cm constant; kinect blob re-centered (x=335). Raw: doc/sources/2026-10-25-swing90-run.md
2026-10-25 repeat run: trajectory repeats within +-10 ticks after start-offset alignment; color reproduces within 1-2 counts at every pose; return 91 ticks (vs 6) - honest bound +-100 ticks (±0.8 deg), set by the recenter. Both runs fit blob_x = 320 + (enc-401)*0.092 -> TRUE CENTER = encoder ~+401 (the backlash midpoint); blob hysteresis ~12-15 px between approaches. The per-frame ratio cross-check failed on encoder timestamp skew - interpolate the encoder at frame times next time; 125 ticks/deg stands on the optical method.

title: Turret homing via color sensor index (cable at camera-forward)
description: Homing: swing toward center watching PORT_1 color; stop on sustained deviation; record encoder = forward reference; track absolute turret angle via encoder + 125 ticks/deg (measured). OPEN: first detected feature (enc -3468) does not match expected cable position - identify landmarks by re-crossing at the same encoder value. Turret travel is cable-limited - never rotate unbounded. Evidence: doc/sources/2026-10-25-turret-calibration.md
notes:
2026-10-25 homing run: obstacle (sonar 75 cm dead-ahead) centered on the Kinect at encoder +527, color ~790 at center (gradient fingerprint, not a step). Sonar never changes with turret angle (chassis-fixed) - it is the distance oracle. Ratio discrepancy (125 far-scene vs ~165-198 near-field implied) = parallax; 125 stands pending a distant-target measurement. Turret now ~6 deg left of center (enc +1268). fd-leak fix deployed (get_voltage SMBus close) - was the true telemetry-death root cause.
2026-10-25 centering run: landmark REPRODUCES but depends on approach direction - left approach centered at enc +527, right approach at +271-275: gear backlash ~252 ticks (~2 deg at 125 ticks/deg). V2 homing must approach from one direction or model the backlash. Tilt -8.5deg moved the obstacle depth reading from 0.79m to 0.70m (sonar 75cm) - down-tilt improves distance agreement.
2026-10-25: the homing MUST handle the cable wrap state - today the tether wedged at ~155 deg CW of camera-forward after the tests wound it 187 deg. The homing intent needs the absolute envelope check + the stall abort (see koc-v2-motord-driver + doc/sources/2026-10-25-turret-cable-incident.md). The physical cable check/free is the user's task before any further rotation.

title: motord: Rust BrickPi+ UART driver prototype (protocol parity vs BrickPi.py)
description: Implement the BrickPi+ protocol in Rust over serialport-rs: 500kbaud /dev/ttyS0, framing [dest][checksum][count][payload] (tx) / [checksum][count][payload] (rx), two ATmega destinations (1,2), MSG_TYPE VALUES/E_STOP/TIMEOUT_SETTINGS. Enable the firmware deadman (TIMEOUT_SETTINGS), wire E_STOP to crash handlers, port the US-sensor I2C workaround. Validate with differential tests vs BrickPi.py on the robot. Protocol: doc/architecture/brickpi-interface.md
notes:
2026-10-25 finding from koc-swing90: the v1 100-deep command queue backs up during streaming (10 Hz in, ~3.3/s consumed) and keeps executing after stop - a 1641-tick (13 deg) overshoot. V2 motord must drop stale commands (timestamped, bounded queue) - matches microduck's deadman doctrine.
2026-10-25 odometry constants measured: 161.0 +- 0.2 ticks/cm of travel (0.2 percent spread over three 20 cm legs); the drive PWM->speed is non-linear (5.1 ticks/s/unit at 25, 7.2 at 50 on the turret, ~1.16 on the drive at 45 - calibrate per motor); GoForward = the left encoder negative / the right positive.
2026-10-25 PHASE 1 MILESTONE: read parity EXACT (A=-7500 B=0 C=297 D=8914 bit-for-bit vs BrickPi.py); motion parity (PWM51 twitch 315 vs 289 ticks); firmware deadman 300ms verified via SIGKILL drill. KEY PROTOCOL FACT: the VALUES response packs ALL 5-bit count fields first, THEN all value fields (BrickPiM EncodeValues) - our first decode interleaved them. Encoder B (unconnected port) reads 0. Drive rate CORRECTED: ~6-8 ticks/s per PWM unit (the old 1.16 was a units error). Build: on-device rustup armv7, 2min, zero-dep (libc only). Remaining: turret parity, estop drill, homing intent, probe-shim acceptance.
2026-10-25 CABLE INCIDENT: the parity tests wound the tether ~187 deg; the recovery hit the stall BOTH directions (13-55 ticks/s vs ~600 free; the battery 8.872 V - not the variable). The robot idle, the turret at ~19771. NEW PHASE-1 REQUIREMENTS: (1) the absolute cable envelope as a first-class motord constraint (the intents beyond it rejected; the envelope re-calibrated after the physical freeing); (2) the in-daemon stall detection (|d(enc)|/dt collapse -> cut the intent + the stall event); (3) the intent refresh must be a dedicated 10 Hz stream (the probe's coupled refresh caused the crawl misread). The motion parity itself PROVEN: the motord 602/s vs the v1 612/s at pwm 82; the v1 swing repeatability 6 ticks. Full capture: doc/sources/2026-10-25-turret-cable-incident.md
2026-10-25 TURRET RECOVERY COMPLETE: the guarded bursts returned the turret to camera-forward (C=45215 vs the target 45297, -0.66 deg; the wrap 359.3 deg of one turn - under the user's limit). ROOT CAUSE OF THE FALSE STALLS: the probe's stall guard divided by a corrupted clock (the post-motion overhead included) AND the snapshot polls starved the intent refresh below the 400 ms expiry - the user called the stall-guard bug correctly. NEW v2 FINDING: the RPC telemetry path stalls pathologically under load (the measured snapshot latencies 0.2-30.7 s during motion; the control intents unaffected, refresh_fails=0, UART errors=0) - the v2 telemetry MUST have timeouts and never share locks with the control loop. The turret rate: ~600 ticks/s at pwm 82 (the parity holds); the stall guard now uses the honest dC/burst_s window.

title: Kinect capture wedge: unthrottled loop + fork-inherited ZMQ fds stall server telemetry
description: KinectProcess (multiprocessing fork) is started after the parent server has created its ZMQ context/sockets, so the child inherits copies of them (visible in ss output: child owns fds on :5557). The capture loop is also unthrottled: 5.7 GB pushed to the aggregator in 33 min at 139% CPU. After some minutes the aggregator stops publishing (360 KB stranded unread in its TCP recv buffer) and BrickPiWrapper stops sending, with no Python errors logged. Restarting server.py recovers. Kinect also sits behind two USB hubs causing libfreenect resync storms (log spam, likely contributes). Fix: throttle capture loop (sleep to ~10-15 fps), fork Kinect before creating parent ZMQ sockets or use spawn, move Kinect to a dedicated USB port. Evidence: doc/sources/2026-10-24-robot-state-capture.md
notes:
2026-10-25: spawn context + 10 fps throttle deployed (app/server/kinect_process.py rewritten). New findings: orphaned spawn children survive restarts (SIGTERM does not reap daemon children - restart must also pkill multiprocessing.spawn); the Kinect USB link via the two-hub chain enters chronic resync storms (Stream 70) within minutes of streaming, spinning the child at ~135% and jamming the aggregator (5557 fills to HWM, telemetry dies). Physical fix required: Kinect on a dedicated USB port. Watcher logging endurance at /tmp/koc_stream_watch.log on the robot.
2026-10-25 constraint from user: the Kinect MUST stay on the hub chain - it provides power the RPi3 port cannot supply (direct port not an option). Root cause refined: two hub hops in series + ~25 MB/s constant wire load on the shared 480 Mbps root bus + power sharing. Mitigation options: single quality powered hub; demand-driven capture in v2 camerad; self-healing worker for v1.
Self-healing deployed and validated: watchdog exits the child on 10s frame stall, reaper respawns in <=3s (kill test passed); SIGTERM handler prevents orphan children. Chronic Storm-70 degradation still expected on the hub chain - recovery now costs seconds, not the server.
SECOND root cause found+fixed 2026-10-25: get_voltage() leaked one SMBus fd per call -> Too many open files killed the BrickPiWrapper thread in ~15-20 min -> telemetry gone. Fixed with a with-block (closed per read); deployed.

title: Probes: drop 360 ticks/rev assumption and duplicate turret ratio constants
description: The BrickPi encoder is 720 ticks/motor rev. Wrong or duplicated in code: testing/turret_ratio_probe.py (docstring says ticks/deg == motor revs per turret rev at 360 ticks/rev; prints that as 'gear ratio'), testing/turret_calibration_probe.py ('gear ratio ... ticks / 360' prints), testing/drive_ratio_probe.py (report line '360 ticks/rev motor ... 17 cm diameter'), testing/turret_envelope.py and turret_homing_probe.py/turret_swing90_probe.py (hard-coded 116.7 / 125 ticks/deg). Single source for values: doc/architecture/robot-hardware.md#measured-constants. Needs a plan in doc/plans before changing code.

title: Drive-ratio probe: count leg ticks rest-to-rest
description: testing/drive_ratio_probe.py drive_ticks() returns the encoder delta at the stop command; the tracks coast ~100-150 more ticks before the Kinect measures the rest position, so its ticks/cm is ~3.5% low (161 vs 166.6 rest-to-rest). Also: back-leg ticks/cm is never computed (travel_b compares to d_ref), and the report line assumes 360 ticks/rev (BrickPi is 720). Evidence: doc/sources/2026-10-26-drive-ratio-rerun.md. Needs a plan in doc/plans before changing code.

title: motord: unlink the UDS socket on SIGINT/SIGTERM exit
description: on_signal() writes E_STOP and _exit(0)s without removing /tmp/motord.sock, so clients that test for the file see a dead daemon (ECONNREFUSED). The probe now tests a real connect (2026-10-26) but the daemon should unlink the socket itself (async-signal-safe unlink(2) of a pre-built CString path). Acceptance: after SIGTERM the socket path does not exist; robotctl status fails fast with not-running.
